ev.q: CDC analyzed pooled 2017–2021 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data to estimate the prevalence of diagnosed arthritis
Approximately one third of veterans had diagnosed arthritis (unadjusted prevalence = 34.7% [men] and 31.9% [women]).
Approximately one third of veterans had diagnosed arthritis
among men aged 18–44 years, arthritis prevalence among veterans (12.7%) was double that of nonveterans (6.2%; PR = 2.1; 95% CI = 1.9–2.2)
Age-standardized diagnosed arthritis prevalences among male and female veterans and nonveterans were estimated in the 50 states, DC, and U.S. territories.
the data are cross-sectional; therefore, a causative relationship between military service and the development of arthritis cannot be inferred.

methods_quotes.q: Crude, age-specific, and age-standardized prevalences of diagnosed arthritis were estimated overall and by veteran status
T-tests were used to assess differences between veterans and nonveterans overall and by subgroup
Prevalence ratios (PRs) were calculated by dividing the prevalence of arthritis among veterans by the prevalence of arthritis among nonveterans.
SAS (version 9.4; SAS Institute) and SUDAAN (version 11.0; RTI International) were used for analysis to account for complex design and weighting.
Estimates are not included because they might be unreliable when the number of respondents is <50 or absolute CI width is >30%.
